# Navigation and Spatial Decision Support

> **Draft chapter map.** Treat navigation as a budgeted engine service: it turns changing spatial data into usable movement decisions without making every AI system own a pathfinder.

## Navigation Is an Engine Service

- Distinguish navigation from steering, decision making, collision, and rigid-body simulation.
- Explain why a path query needs a stable spatial representation, filtering policy, and result contract before choosing an algorithm.

### Pathfinding Is Not AI

- Separate a request for a traversable route from the gameplay choice of where and when an agent should move.
- Compare navigation meshes, grids, waypoint graphs, voxel volumes, and hybrid representations in terms of the worlds they model well.

#### The Query Contract

- Define agent capability, start and goal, filters, partial paths, failure, and cancellation as explicit query data.
- Explain why the game-facing World asks for a decision while the navigation service owns its acceleration structures.

## Navigation Data at World Scale

- Connect authored navigation, procedural terrain, destruction, and streamed cells to a changing spatial index.
- Explain the difference between building navigation data, loading it, and incrementally repairing it.

### Building, Streaming, and Updating

- Cover tiles, regions, portals, off-mesh links, and invalidation boundaries.
- Relate residency and versioning to the World-streaming contracts from Chapter 11.

#### Threading and Budget Policy

- Explain why long searches and rebuilds need queues, cancellation, priorities, and per-frame work budgets.
- Establish result age and world-version checks so a route computed yesterday is not silently applied to a changed world.

## Request, Result, and World Change

- Show how systems submit requests, observe completed results, and react to a blocked or changed route.
- Keep result delivery asynchronous so pathfinding cannot stall simulation or compete unpredictably with rendering.

### Navigation Across Domains

- Connect navigation to physics queries, streaming, animation locomotion, networking, and debug visualization.
- Explain how shared vocabulary and narrow adapters avoid a single all-knowing spatial subsystem.

#### Smallworld Direction

- Use Smallworld to illustrate a concrete Rust service, its ownership boundaries, and the budgets it exposes.
- Separate the durable service design from any one navigation crate or world representation.
